title: Aji de Gallina
subtitle: shredded chicken in walnut and aji amarillo cream sauce
excerpt: Aji de gallina is a rich Peruvian chicken dish with a golden sauce made from aji amarillo, walnuts, bread and cream. Shredded chicken is folded through the sauce and served over rice with black olives and hard-boiled eggs. It is one of the most comforting dishes in the Peruvian home cooking repertoire.
sourceNotes: Aji de gallina is one of the great comfort dishes of Peruvian home cooking, with roots in the colonial-era dish called manjar blanco, which used chicken, almonds and cream. Over time the recipe was adapted using local aji amarillo chilli and walnuts, becoming the creamy yellow dish recognised today.

glossaryTerms.definition: A bright orange Peruvian chilli with a fruity, moderate heat. It is one of the most important ingredients in Peruvian cooking and forms the base of many sauces and stews. Available as a paste in Latin food shops.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and takes about 1 hour in total, including poaching the chicken. The sauce is built around
paste, blended with walnuts, milk-soaked bread and evaporated milk to create a thick, golden, nutty cream that clings to every piece of shredded chicken.

Blend the walnut and bread mixture until completely smooth before adding it to the pan. Any lumps left in the sauce will be obvious in the finished dish. If the sauce thickens too much as it cooks, loosen it with a splash of the chicken poaching liquid, which adds flavour as well as body.

Place the chicken thighs in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 25 to 30 minutes until cooked through. Remove the chicken and reserve the poaching liquid. Once cool enough to handle, remove the skin and bones and shred the meat into strips.
Soak 4 slices of white bread with the crusts removed in 150ml of the evaporated milk or double cream for 5 minutes. Blend with 100g walnuts until completely smooth. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the aji amarillo paste and 1 tsp cumin to the pan. Stir and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.

Pour in the walnut and bread paste along with the remaining evaporated milk. Stir well and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring frequently. The sauce will thicken as it cooks. Loosen with poaching liquid if needed.
Fold the shredded chicken into the sauce and heat through for 3 to 4 minutes. Taste and season with salt.
Serve over cooked long-grain rice. Garnish with halved hard-boiled eggs and black olives.

attrs.cause: The walnut and bread mixture was not blended long enough
attrs.fix: Blend for a full 2 minutes and pass through a sieve if any texture remains before adding to the pan.

attrs.symptom: Sauce is too thick and stodgy
attrs.cause: Too much bread was used or the sauce was reduced too long
attrs.fix: Add poaching liquid a splash at a time, stirring over low heat until you reach a coating consistency.

attrs.cause: Not enough aji amarillo paste or the paste was not cooked out
attrs.fix: Fry the paste in the oil with the onion for at least 2 minutes before adding the other ingredients. Taste and add more paste if needed.

content.text: Aji de gallina is a Sunday lunch dish across Peru. It appears at family tables and in small neighbourhood restaurants. The golden sauce and the combination of eggs and olives make it easy to spot on a plate.
